summary: Catskill tower: the register says built 1917, the DEC says 1927 on Gallis Hill and at its present location since 1950; restored and reopened 1999 with weekend volunteers.

facts.design: 60-foot steel Aermotor LS-40 tower with a 7 by 7 foot metal cab (register: 7’x 7’ metal cab)

staffing.status: volunteer on duty weekends and holidays since the 1999 reopening

access.note: reached by a 5-6 mile hike on the Overlook Spur Trail; volunteers on duty weekends and holidays; motor vehicle access by permit (CP-3) was proposed in a draft plan and opposed by the FFLA in a December 15, 2016 letter

visit.trail_note: five to six miles on the Overlook Spur Trail, moderate to difficult, per the DEC

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The National Historic Lookout Register says the tower was constructed by the state Department of Conservation in 1917. The DEC challenge page says it was originally constructed in 1927 on Gallis Hill and at its present location since 1950. The story reports both and does not choose one.
The register gives 3,120 ft (951 m) and the DEC gives 3,140 feet for the same summit. The story gives both figures.

notes_for_editor: Built year is disputed (register 1917 vs DEC 1927, with the tower at its present location since 1950 per DEC). The 1971 closing year comes only from the register; a search snippet pointed to a 1988 closure at catskillsvisitorcenter.org, but that page returned HTTP 403 and was not used. andyarthur.org (403), catskillcenter.org (404), and a firetower.org page (404) could not be read. Public access is by a 5-6 mile hike (DEC). Vehicle access by permit (CP-3) was a draft-plan proposal that the FFLA opposed in a letter dated December 15, 2016 to NYSDEC. The register's 'Staffed? No' refers to Forest Service staffing; the volunteer weekend presence is from the register text. Fact-check 2026-10-08: 'small' cab and 'hotel' were removed as unsupported; the story now gives the register's 7 by 7 foot cab.
